title: Barcode Scanning, One-Click Imports, and a Faster Way In
summary: Version 3.1 is mostly about the phone: barcode scanning that works inside an installed app, importers so switching trackers does not mean starting from an empty log, and an Android build with in-app Pro. Plus the launch and sign-in path, which had been dropping people on the marketing page and making them think they had been signed out.
highlights: Barcode scanning on your phone: point the camera at a label and the food goes in, with the two policy bugs fixed that were stopping an installed app from using the camera at all
One-click imports from MyFitnessPal, Cronometer, MacroFactor and Lose It!, so moving over does not start from an empty log
Shareable macro snapshots: a rendered scorecard of your day, drawn on your own device
The installed app now opens on your log instead of the marketing page, and no longer sits on a spinner when it starts with no connection
Signing in costs one round trip instead of two, with 150ms of fixed delay taken out of the path
An Android build with in-app Pro through Google Play Billing. Not on the Play Store yet — the listing is still being set up
Health data stays out of browser storage, and biometric unlock is opt-in and cleared when you sign out
Migration guides for anyone moving from another tracker, and a comparison hub covering the alternatives
Blog posts and comparison pages are pre-rendered, so a cold load and a search crawler both get real content instead of a flash of fallback
Macro percentages no longer clip out of the reporting card, navigation resets the scroll position, and logout moved into Settings
The support address on the privacy policy, the terms and the footer works again. It had been shipping as a placeholder that could not receive mail

title: One Design System, End to End
summary: Version 3 closes a design system that had drifted into twenty surface fills, seven corner radii and three separate page headers, and fixes a long list of things that were quietly not working underneath it.
highlights: A closed token set: four surfaces, two hairlines, three radii, one focus ring, replacing roughly twenty ad-hoc alpha variants
A brand derived from the logo artwork rather than a saturated default, on a warm near-black page instead of pure #000
Macros read green, blue and yellow, so no macronutrient shares a colour with the primary action or the error state
One header, one panel, one tab bar, one disclosure and one empty state across the app and the public site
A mobile tab bar with the log action in the thumb zone, and a log sheet that opens wherever you are
Corrected activity multipliers: sedentary was 1.0, which made TDEE identical to BMR
Select chevrons, icon button shapes, toast stacking and the FAQ animation all fixed for browsers other than Chrome
Offline navigation, a real install prompt, safe-area handling and one chrome colour for the installed app
The landing page now shows the product working, using the same charts the app renders
A typecheck that actually runs: the script compiled nothing, hiding 38 real errors including four defects in Google sign-in

title: Free Nutrition Calculators & Organic Discovery
highlights: Five free calculators at /tools: TDEE, BMR, macro split, weight loss timeline, and protein intake
No account required, every calculator runs entirely in the browser
New Tools menu in the header and a calculator hub with cross-linking
Structured data and sitemap coverage so the calculators are discoverable in search
Container images now published to Docker Hub alongside GHCR, for both amd64 and arm64

title: Mobile Layout Polish & Compact UX
highlights: Optimized mobile layout density across Goals, Analytics, and Settings pages
Compact 3-column mobile stats grid and daily macro breakdown
Refined form input ghost text, search buttons, and button scaling
Sleek mobile navigation menu with active page highlights
Automatic www domain redirect to main domain (301 Permanent Redirect)
